clue.text: Very quietly, not closing mouth, making one nod

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: not closing tells us the word for mouth loses its final letter

parts.note: an orifice is an opening such as a mouth

explanation.surface: Someone gapes in a silent yawn and drifts off in their chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not closing' removes the last letter E from ORIFICE, leaving ORIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sleep-inducing makes a listener doze off, nodding their head.

clue.text: Virgin, for example, making rude demand for famous autograph?

definitions.meaning: the Virgin is Virgo, one of the zodiac signs

definitions.text: making rude demand for famous autograph?
definitions.meaning: read as a curt order to a celebrity to write their name

explanation.surface: A celebrity is rudely asked for a signature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' looks like the airline or record label, but it is Virgo.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is one of twelve zodiac divisions; the second reading is a blunt command to a celebrity to write their name.

clue.text: Factory schedule is on time

parts.note: a plan is a schedule

explanation.surface: A works timetable runs to schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works where goods are made.

clue.text: During commission, added her name for review

indicators.note: for review suggests the letters are reworked and examined afresh

explanation.surface: A committee member slips her name into a document awaiting review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commission' looks like a committee, but it means the committing of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in the act of a crime means caught while carrying it out.

clue.text: Noted performance of chess people putting up work of art

parts.note: FIDE is the international chess federation

indicators.note: putting up in a down clue means the word for work of art is reversed

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: Chess players hang a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes: this is Beethoven's only opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's opera is a musical stage work, a performance in notes.

clue.text: Has at one time to undergo cold in the morning, and PM

indicators.note: to undergo is read as to go under, so these pieces sit below the cold abbreviation in this down clue

parts.note: hath is the old form of has
am means in the morning

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister once caught a chill in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like afternoon, paired with the morning, but it is a Prime Minister: Pitt the Elder became Earl of Chatham.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt the Elder, Earl of Chatham, was a British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Come back, concerned with solution being incomplete

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: being incomplete says the word for solution is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a cure is a remedy or solution to a problem

explanation.surface: Someone returns to an unfinished remedy they were worried about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being incomplete' drops the final E of CURE to give CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again is to return, so a recurring event comes back.

clue.text: Prepare to deliver son at last amid physical collapse

indicators.note: amid says that letter goes inside the word for collapse

parts.note: ruin is a building's collapse

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of son is taken

explanation.surface: A midwife readies a birth amid physical exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliver' suggests childbirth, but a new car is driven gently before full use or handover.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving a new engine gently at first readies it before handing over or working hard.

clue.text: Fried dish of game: taste only the outside

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game with mallets

indicators.note: only the outside means just the first and last letters of taste are used

explanation.surface: A fried meal of game where only the crust is tasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like game meat in a dish, but it is a lawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small fried roll of mashed food in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Anorak is hooded, somewhat jaunty

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hooded anorak looks rather dashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish means dashing and stylish, worn at a jaunty angle.

clue.text: Turning to pick out a prize

indicators.note: turning tells us the words for pick out and a are read backwards together

parts.note: to draw is to pick out, as names from a hat

explanation.surface: Someone turns to select a winner from the entrants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning to' reads as turning towards someone, but it is the reversal signal for everything after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize, a trophy given to a winner.

clue.text: Haggard with effort, one with a lot of needle

definitions.text: one with a lot of needle

parts.note: drawn means looking tired and haggard
work is effort or labour

explanation.surface: An exhausted person struggles, and someone else is full of irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' looks like bad feeling (British slang for antagonism), but it is the sewing needle: this is a kind of embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn-thread embroidery is decorative stitching that needs a great deal of sewing by hand.

clue.text: Prepare to depart, as teams don't do so well

parts.note: sets are groups or teams, as in a tennis or social set
to ail is to be unwell, not doing well

explanation.surface: Squads are struggling and getting ready to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoisting canvas and putting out to sea is how a ship begins a voyage.

clue.text: Long time kept in working to such a degree

indicators.note: kept in tells us the word for working is placed inside the word for long time

parts.note: hours suggests a long time, as in 'it took hours'
on means working or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: An employee is made to stay late at work to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to such a degree' looks like 'to this extent', but a university degree is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A British first or second-class university qualification is classified with this distinction.

clue.text: Inside borders of Germany, a tough Marxist has not succeeded creating safe houses

indicators.note: Inside says the rest goes within those two border letters
borders of means only the first and last letters of Germany are used

parts.note: a Ted (Teddy boy) was a 1950s British young tough

indicators.note: has not tells us the word for Marxist lacks the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a communist is a Marxist
s is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A hard-line Marxist in Germany fails to build secure housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has not succeeded' reads as the Marxist failing, but it removes the genealogical S; the leftovers sit 'Inside' the first and last letters of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A fenced estate with controlled entry offers residents protected homes.

clue.text: So many of you on the beaches?

parts.note: thou is the old form of you
sands are beaches

explanation.surface: A huge crowd of you on the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers in the high hundreds and beyond describe a vast quantity.

clue.text: No red meat, ordered church

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner orders a meal with no red meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing a food order.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Paris cathedral is a famous Gothic church.

clue.text: Giant moose run amok

indicators.note: running amok means wild disorder, so the letters scatter

explanation.surface: A huge elk charges wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means huge, vast in size.

clue.text: Keeping model aeroplanes, stacks of them

parts.note: holding means keeping
a pattern is a model to copy

explanation.surface: A hobbyist keeps piles of model planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model aeroplanes' reads as a hobby, but 'model' is a separate piece and the planes are real ones circling an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft waiting to land circle in layers above an airport, which controllers call a stack.

clue.text: Making observation about husband's love

indicators.note: about says the word for making observation goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: noting means observing or remarking

explanation.surface: Someone comments on a husband's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a score of zero is called love.

clue.text: Indian city supports school in painful condition

indicators.note: supports in a down clue puts the city beneath the other piece

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Indian city backs a school in a medical emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Podagra is gout affecting the foot, a painful joint disease.

clue.text: Supple mountaineer heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a climber is a mountaineer

explanation.surface: A flexible mountaineer sets out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes C from the start of CLIMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Limber means flexible and lithe.

clue.text: Understanding night is falling

indicators.note: falling suggests the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Dusk descends and the darkness comes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is perception or deep comprehension of something.

clue.text: Poet admitting verse is something saucy

indicators.note: admitting means letting the verse abbreviation inside the poet's name

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A poet confesses his verse is risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' suggests cheeky, but it means sauce-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is a meat sauce, something literally sauce-like.

clue.text: Theatre worker, one getting clobbered

definitions.meaning: a backstage helper who looks after actors' costumes
clobber is British slang for clothes, so this is someone putting on garments

explanation.surface: A stagehand is the one who takes a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobbered' suggests being hit, but clobber is British slang for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume assistant in the theatre helps performers into outfits, and anyone clothing themselves is likewise getting into gear.

clue.text: Beat son, tiny boy

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone hits a little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To smite is to strike hard.

clue.text: Players getting on to some first aid

parts.note: a band is a group of musical players
aging means getting on in years

explanation.surface: Musicians growing old need a little medical attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping a wound in strips of dressing is a basic treatment for injuries.

clue.text: I'm a fighter, old friend

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being a fighter and of an old companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm a fighter' reads as a boast, but the jet is speaking: 'I'm a MiG'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for a pal or comrade, used informally in English too.

clue.text: State television's not a good bet

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
Sky is a British satellite television company

explanation.surface: A state broadcaster is a poor investment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazardous venture is a dangerous gamble, unwise to wager on.

clue.text: Good to cut down on running, if awkward

indicators.note: on here means the cutting down is applied after running, so that word comes second

parts.note: a race is a running contest
doing less of something is cutting down

explanation.surface: An athlete is told to train less if they move clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking poise or elegance means clumsy and ungainly.
